cards.explanation: The answer is don't leave out a single word. The LORD tells Jeremiah, "Do not omit a word." (Jeremiah 26:2) Every word stays in, friends. Skip the chocolate chips and that's not the recipe anymore. Jeremiah doesn't get to trim the message.

The answer is False. The LORD doesn't say there's no chance. He says, "Perhaps they will listen and turn…" (Jeremiah 26:3) The aim is that they turn from their evil way of life, so that He may relent of the disaster He is planning. Perhaps is a small word, bakers, but it's holding a big door open.

The word is cursing. The LORD says He will make the city "…an object of cursing among all the nations of the earth." (Jeremiah 26:6) That's a heavy line, friends. It's the picture of what's at stake if the people won't listen.

The answer is that they seize him and shout for his death. The priests, the prophets and all the people seized Jeremiah, shouting, "You must surely die!" (Jeremiah 26:8) This part of the story is heavy, and I think it hurts to read it. Jeremiah had just finished saying everything the LORD commanded, and it turned on him that fast.

The answer is desolate and deserted. The crowd says Jeremiah dared to prophesy that "…this city will be desolate and deserted!" (Jeremiah 26:9) They say it right to his face, friends. They repeat his message back at him, and I bet they are not happy about it.

The answer is that they heard it with their own ears. The priests and prophets tell the officials and the people that they know it "…as you have heard with your own ears!" (Jeremiah 26:11) That's their claim, bakers. No middleman, just ears.

The answer is True. The priests and prophets say the man is worthy of death "…for he has prophesied against this city…" (Jeremiah 26:11) That's the reason they give, friends. Plain and simple, they point to what he said about the city.

The answer is to correct their ways and obey the LORD. Jeremiah says, "…correct your ways and deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD your God…" (Jeremiah 26:13) His own life is on the line and he's still urging them to turn. He keeps pointing the crowd back to the LORD instead of at himself.

The word is innocent. Jeremiah says, "…you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city, and upon its residents…" (Jeremiah 26:15) I think he's calm about it, even with a crowd around him. It's a serious warning, friends.

The answer is that this man is not worthy of death. The officials and all the people tell the priests and prophets, "This man is not worthy of death…" (Jeremiah 26:16) That's a big turn from the shouting earlier, bakers. And they say it straight to the priests and prophets.

The answer is that Zion will be plowed like a field. The elders say Micah told all Judah, "Zion will be plowed like a field…" (Jeremiah 26:18) Micah the Moreshite was a prophet in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah. He gave a hard message too, friends, and the elders bring it up on purpose.

The answer is False. The elders ask, "Did Hezekiah king of Judah or anyone else in Judah put him to death?" (Jeremiah 26:19) Nothing in the text has anyone putting Micah to death. The elders say Hezekiah feared the LORD and sought His favor.

The answer is True. The elders finish with, "But we are about to bring great harm on ourselves!" (Jeremiah 26:19) They look at what the assembly is about to do and say it out loud. I think that's a brave thing to say to a crowd, friends.

The answer is that the king tries to put him to death. The text says, "…the king sought to put him to death." (Jeremiah 26:21) King Jehoiakim and his mighty men and officials heard Uriah's words. It's a heavy part of the story, friends.
The word is fear. The text says, "…he fled in fear and went to Egypt." (Jeremiah 26:21) Uriah son of Shemaiah heard what the king wanted and ran. I think anyone would feel that kind of fear, bakers.

The answer is Ahikam son of Shaphan. The text says, "Nevertheless, Ahikam son of Shaphan supported Jeremiah, so he was not handed over to the people to be put to death." (Jeremiah 26:24) Everybody needs somebody on their side when the room turns cold, friends. For Jeremiah, that was Ahikam.
